desc:
You are given an array nums of positive integers and a non-negative integer d. Choose two different positions i and j such that the two values differ by at most d, that is |nums[i] - nums[j]| ≤ d, and the sum nums[i] + nums[j] is as large as possible.

Return that largest sum, or -1 if no two elements differ by at most d.

nums = [2, 9, 5, 12, 3], d = 2
sorted: 2 3 5 9 12
best pair is (3, 5)  ->  result = 8

nums = [5, 3, 8], d = 0
result = -1
hints: Checking all pairs is O(n²). Sort the array and think about which pairs could ever be optimal.
Take any valid pair x ≤ y in the sorted array. If there is an element between them, or just below y, can you swap x for it?

A valid pair can always be replaced by the pair formed by y and its sorted predecessor: that predecessor is at least x and closer to y. So only adjacent pairs matter; scan from the top and return the first adjacent pair whose difference is at most d.
editorial: Sort the array. Suppose (a[p], a[q]) with p < q is a valid pair. Then (a[q-1], a[q]) is also valid, because a[q-1] ≥ a[p] makes the difference no larger, and its sum is no smaller. Hence an optimal pair can always be chosen from adjacent elements of the sorted array.

Among adjacent pairs, the sum a[j-1] + a[j] grows with j, so the best valid one is the highest index j with a[j] - a[j-1] ≤ d. Walk j down from the end and stop at the first success; if the loop finishes, the answer is -1. After the O(n log n) sort the scan is O(n).
